title: Private VPC: evidence-driven upgrade safeguards and acceptance criteria
creator: Maria Chen
description: Problem: Private/VPC customers require predictable, auditable upgrades that work in constrained networking environments (zero/limited egress, mirror-based artifact distribution) while minimizing downtime and operator interventions. This ticket defines a set of evidence-driven safeguards, deterministic checks, and acceptance criteria for operator-driven and automated upgrades in Private deployments. The goal is to provide a prescriptive upgrade contract customers can depend on, reduce upgrade-induced incidents, and enable safe rollouts for air-gapped and minimal-egress environments.
background: We have repeated ambiguity in acceptance criteria for 'airgap-compatible' upgrades: what operational steps are required, how to validate artifact integrity without outbound egress, and what constitutes a safe canary in restricted networks. Past incidents (inc-2024-11-region-upgrade) highlighted failure modes from missing artifact checksums and incomplete mirror replication. This PRD consolidates learnings and prescribes evidence that must be collected pre-, during-, and post-upgrade.
scope: In-scope: operator-run image & operator upgrades for Private/VPC clusters, mirror synchronization validation, manifest-driven upgrade orchestration, deterministic preflight checks, canary traffic design for constrained networks, rollback triggers and post-upgrade evidence collection. Out-of-scope: Hosted API upgrades, Dedicated multi-tenant pool upgrades, customer-specific operator code changes.
non_goals: Provide a one-size-fits-all on-prem package for arbitrary hardware; replace customer operator automation; expand to productized managed upgrades for air-gapped customers (this is a spec to enable those features later).
acceptance_criteria: Preflight manifest validation: upgrade manifest contains artifact URIs, PGP signatures, and SHA256 checksums; operator tool verifies signatures and checksums against local mirror storage before any node changes.

Zero-external-egress verification mode: documented path to perform the full upgrade using only local mirrors (no DNS resolution to external registries). Acceptance requires a recorded preflight log demonstrating all artifacts resolved from local mirrors.

Deterministic canary: canary rollout is limited to <=5% of control-plane/serving nodes or to a single replica set; canary success metrics are compared to baseline using predefined metric anchors (error rate, p50/p95 latency, throughput). Canary rollout must automatically pause on metric regression exceeding thresholds defined in the manifest.

Atomic rollback trigger: automated rollback to prior images must be executable within the upgrade playbook if canary or post-rollout checks fail. Rollback execution must be reversible and leave an attestation log explaining root cause trigger.
Checksum reconciliation report: post-sync job produces a reconciliation artifact listing any mismatched checksums between mirror and source artifacts and flags unacceptable mismatches as blockers.
KMS key rotation safe path: acceptance demonstrates that KMS rotations (customer-managed) do not block operator upgrades; playbook includes key-rotation verification steps and failure mitigation.

Observability & audit: all upgrade steps emit structured audit events to the Private control plane (or local audit store) that include operator, timestamp, manifest ID, artifact checksums, and canary metric snapshots. Example events must be present in test run logs.
Operator manual-fallback: documented and tested manual fallback steps for scenarios where automated rollback cannot complete due to partial network partitions or operator node drain failures.

Test matrix coverage: upgrade scenarios tested in CI include: normal egress, mirror-only (no egress), partial mirror replication (missing artifact), and simulated partition mid-upgrade. Results are attached to the PR as evidence.
Customer-facing runbook: concise upgrade runbook and checklist (<= 2 pages) produced for customers with step-by-step preflight, mirror sync, canary validation, and rollback procedures.
decisions: Adopt manifest-driven upgrades as the canonical format for Private upgrades: manifests include artifact list, checksums, signatures, and metric thresholds.
Require signed manifests (PGP or comparable) for any air-gapped upgrade; unsigned artifacts allowed only for experimental/test clusters with explicit warnings.
Canary scope defaulted to single-replica or <=5% of capacity; teams may override with explicit documented risk acceptance.
Observability contract: even when control-plane telemetry is restricted, attestations must be stored locally and exportable for post-mortem review.
Do not implement a centralized SaaS-based health validator for air-gapped customers; validators will run locally with optional signed evidence upload if customer permits egress.
Treat checksum mismatches as blockers for production upgrades; allow manual operator override in non-production/test contexts with explicit logging.
Integrate the upgrade preflight into the private operator CLI with an exit code semantics compatible with CI (0 = pass, non-zero = fail) to enable automated gating in customer pipelines.
Provide a minimal 'egress-emulation' harness for offline testing environments to simulate missing mirrors and partial replication during CI tests.
Expose a short JSON attestation artifact that can be submitted to Redwood support for forensic debugging; artifact contains manifest ID, checksums, operator identity, and metric snapshots.

Timing SLA: full cluster upgrade must present an estimated time window; acceptance requires improved operator guidance to keep customer downtime within declared windows or perform rolling upgrades with no traffic loss for stateless components.
Include 'graceful-degradation' mappings for known optional components (telemetry, metrics-forwarder) so that lack of connectivity to those components does not block core upgrade path.
Require security review before rollout to customers with sensitive regulatory controls (PCI, HIPAA) as part of release gating.
Default mirror verification to use SHA256 and fall back to SHA512 only when explicitly provided.
Instruct engineering to keep the manifest schema stable (v1) with a documented upgrade path for schema v2 to avoid breaking offline validators.
Adopt a golden-baseline metric snapshot approach for canary comparison, stored as a compact time-series snapshot in the upgrade artifact bundle.
Define failure severity mapping: metric regressions that increase error rate by > 0.5% are P0 and auto-pause the rollout; latency regressions p95 > baseline * 2.0 are P0 as well.
Require an on-call engineering verification window (2 business days) after GA of the upgrade contract to monitor early adopters and collect feedback.
Do not mandate physical media delivery workflows here; those are covered by a separate PM ticket focused on media-based artifact distribution.
Ship minimal UX changes to the Console for Private customers in an opt-in beta to display attestation artifacts and upgrade logs.
Provide an 'audit-only' dry-run mode which creates all attestation artifacts and logs without mutating cluster state to provide evidence for customers before committing.
Default to rolling upgrades for control plane components in Private deployments with strict drain timeouts and health-check gating.
Require explicit allowlist entries for network ports and domains needed for optional pre-flight artifact validation if customer chooses egress-enabled preflight.
Accept a small, well-documented set of operator privileges required to run preflight and upgrade steps; minimize required privileges where possible.
Forbid any plaintext secret transport during mirror sync; all artifacts and keys must be transferred using encrypted channels or signed and verified locally.
Integrate the upgrade preflight with Redwood Optimize recommendations to suggest quantization-compatible model variants when model artifacts are part of the upgrade bundle.
Allow customers to tag clusters as 'strict-airgap' which enforces the strictest verification path and blocks any override without multi-actor approval.
Define a minimal telemetry envelope that can be optionally exported post-upgrade when customers grant temporary egress to Redwood support for debugging.
Require an engineering-runbook and a one-hour dry-run with synthetic traffic for any production upgrade that modifies the KV cache format or kernel selection paths.
Default to idempotent upgrade operations in the operator (retries safe by design) to handle flaky networking during mirror fetches.
Set a maximum manual intervention window: if automated rollback or remediation exceeds 2 hours, the operator must escalate to on-call and provide a recovery plan.
Design the attestation artifact to be compact (<= 1MB) for easy transfer in constrained networks and to minimize storage overhead in the customer's audit store.

test_plan: CI: preflight-validator unit tests for manifest parsing, signature verification, and checksum validation.
CI: integration job with ephemeral mirror (mirrord) that simulates network partitions and missing artifacts.
Staging: perform mirror-only upgrade on dedicated staging cluster with synthetic traffic and verify attestation events are generated and stored locally.
Pilot: coordinate with two pilot customers (one strict-airgap, one partial-egress) to execute the full upgrade playbook, collect logs, and confirm runbook accuracy.
Chaos: simulate node drain failure during canary rollout and verify operator idempotency and rollback triggers.
Telemetry: validate that canary metric comparison routine correctly computes deviations and honors configured thresholds in manifest.
Security: KMS rotation simulation and verification that operator does not deadlock when credentials are rotated mid-upgrade.
Compliance: ensure audit artifacts meet minimum retention / immutability needs for regulated customers (samples attached to PR).
rollback_plan: Automated rollback: operator executes kubectl-like manifest revert to prior images and runs post-rollback health-checks; attestation produced indicating rollback reason.
Partial-network fallback: if rollback cannot fetch previous images, operator will instruct to re-point to local mirror copy and re-run verified fetch.
Manual escalation: if automated rollback fails after 2 hours, escalate to on-call SRE with a documented contact list and a playbook to restore customer-facing endpoints.
Data safety: no schema migrations that are irreversible in a single upgrade; any migration requiring irreversible changes must be separated and flagged in manifest.
Communication: notify customer via configured incident channel and attach attestation artifacts and reconciliation report within 30 minutes of rollback start.
Post-rollback analysis: require a postmortem entry in internal tracker and update manifest schema or runbook based on root cause.
risks: Customers mis-configure mirrors leading to missing artifacts at upgrade time (mitigation: preflight mirror-check with checksum reconciliation).
KMS/secret management interactions that prevent operator from decrypting artifacts during upgrade (mitigation: explicit test cases and preflight key-check).
Operator privileges insufficient in some customer environments (mitigation: minimal privilege list and preflight permission validator).
Attestation artifacts containing sensitive metadata must be protected; customers may restrict export (mitigation: encrypted local storage and clear consent model for exports).
False-positive metric regressions due to noisy baselines causing unnecessary rollbacks (mitigation: golden-baseline snapshot and windowed comparisons).
Edge hardware differences in customer clusters could reveal upgrade-time performance regressions (mitigation: pilot customers and descriptive hardware profile in manifest).
Regulatory constraints preventing any egress make live support difficult (mitigation: pre-signed attestations and robust local debugging guidance).
deliverables: Manifest v1 schema and example bundles
Operator preflight CLI with exit codes and logging
CI test jobs covering mirror-only/partial-mirror scenarios
Attestation artifact spec and compact JSON schema
Pilot execution report (for two pilot customers)
Console opt-in view for attestation artifacts (beta)
notes: Keep manifest examples minimal for first release; customers can extend with optional fields.
Coordinate with Legal for required wording in attestation artifact export when customers permit egress to Redwood support.
Pilot customers should represent two distinct operational profiles: a strict-airgap appliance and a cloud-hosted VPC with limited egress.
Follow-up PM ticket will capture physical-media delivery workflows if pilot feedback shows need.
Consider later integration with Redwood Console to display attestation history and preflight results in a timeline view.
Ensure SDK/CLI docs include quick debug commands to inspect mirror contents and to re-run preflight in verbose mode.
